title: Benefits of Reciting the Quran
summary: Reciting the Quran is vital for spiritual well-being and acts as an intercessor. It cleanses the heart and holds higher rewards than supplication. Even those who struggle in recitation are doubly rewarded for their effort. Regular recitation should be part of daily life, aiming to complete portions consistently, helping to revive the heart and reinforce commitment to Islamic teachings.
translation:
Recitation of the Holy Quran should be an integral part of our lives and routines. Through recitation, we gain personal life and significant provisions for the Hereafter, as it will intercede for us with Allah Almighty, testifying on our behalf. This is why Allah commanded the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to mention the virtues of the Quran, highlighting the value and status of a person in Allah's sight.

There is a Hadith: "What Allah does not grant to those who pray in supplication, He gives to those who recite the Quran." Therefore, a person more dedicated to Quran recitation throughout the day than supplicating is said to receive greater rewards. As the Word of Allah, it expresses His greatness and contains His commandments; through recitation, one cleanses their heart of rust, similar to how water rusts iron, making it useless. A rusted heart cannot absorb fear and humility of Allah and becomes insignificant to Him. Like cleaning iron restores its utility, a cleansed heart becomes capable of submitting to Allah.

Heart cleansing involves two things: remembering death and frequent recitation of the Quran. There is significant reward from Allah for frequently reciting the Quran, even for those who stutter, as they receive double the reward: one for the effort and one for the recitation itself. Hence, no expert should consider that someone who stutters receives less reward, nor should a stutterer feel inadequate next to proficient reciters. Even if they stammer, they too are given double reward for their recitation and effort.

Make Quran recitation a routine in life. Before dawn, finish a portion of the Quran, and before sleep, complete another portion. It is best to complete one 'Manzil' daily, or if not possible, three parts, or at least one part should be recited. If that is not feasible, even one page is better than none. Reciting the Quran while looking at it enlightens our eyes, revives our hearts, and renews our promise to follow Shariah commands. May Allah grant us the ability to perform righteous deeds and bless us with a bond with the Holy Quran.
